body:
Founder real-time: "can we start updating more of the standard library
to be pure parena/" -> "there is a lot of c ffi maybe we can replace
some of it". Audited stdlib for the specific real pattern of one
module rolling its own inline-c for something a shared module already
provides in pure PARENA, rather than a broad "purify everything" sweep
(most FFI in this stdlib is genuinely irreducible -- OS syscalls, SDL2,
real crypto libraries -- already following a disciplined "thin #target
primitive + pure PARENA logic on top" pattern established in io.prn's
own prior rewrite).

Found and consolidated 4 confirmed real duplicates:

1. net/http.prn's own i32-to-string (snprintf-based) duplicated
   string.prn's own already-existing i32-to-string byte for byte --
   http.prn's own header comment claiming "string.prn only ships
   parse-i32... not the reverse" was simply stale (string.prn gained
   i32-to-string earlier this session). Deleted, call site switched to
   string/i32-to-string.

2. json.prn and yaml.prn each independently carried an identical
   parse-f64-raw (strtod wrapper), each already doing their own real
   validation before calling it. Consolidated into ONE shared
   string/parse-f64-raw, exported. Named to avoid colliding with
   expr.prn's own real, different, pre-existing raw-parse-f64 (atof,
   not strtod) -- found live via a real gcc "redefinition" error when
   both got compiled together in test-awk, the same "private names
   aren't module-scoped" collision class this session's self-hosting
   work already hit repeatedly.

3. awk.prn and grep.prn each independently carried an identical
   unbox-bool. grep.prn's own original header comment already noted
   the duplication was a deliberate, considered tradeoff at the time
   ("purely for this one call site, grep.prn doesn't export it") --
   consolidated into regex/pcre.prn (a shared dependency both already
   import for is-match itself) now that 2 real call sites need it.

4. editor/textmate.prn's own tm-match-start/tm-match-end were
   byte-for-byte identical to regex/pcre.prn's own private
   match-start-i32/match-end-i32 -- same real Match struct (textmate
   never defines its own; it was always pcre's). Consolidated into
   pcre's own now-exported versions.

Verified each with the real, existing test/build targets that
actually exercise them: test-json, test-yaml, test-awk (real
end-to-end file processing, 10 assertions), turbogrep (real binary,
smoke-tested against a real multi-line file, correct match output),
test-editor-render (real Xvfb SDL2 render, 24 assertions), test-
webdriver (real end-to-end HTTP session against a fake WebDriver
server, 13 assertions). Full local suite (336 tests) + all 5 selfhost
domains clean, zero regressions. CI green on all 4 jobs.

PARENA commit d571624. CI run 33105336829: all 4 jobs green.
